scope: Recommended Security and Confidentiality Type I

controls.control: Management assigns security, privacy, system, and control ownership and approves policies at least annually.
Security responsibilities, incident channels, and material changes are communicated to personnel and relevant external parties.
Management performs and approves a documented security risk assessment covering fraud, vendors, technology, AI, and business change.
Vendors are inventoried, assessed before restricted-data use, contractually governed, monitored, and offboarded.
Production identity is authenticated and authorization is derived server-side with tenant ownership enforced at API and persistence layers.
Privileged access is approved, least-privileged, MFA-protected, reviewed quarterly, and revoked promptly after role change or separation.
Restricted customer information uses private storage, encrypted transport, cache prevention, owner-scoped paths, and controlled deletion.
Confidential information is classified, retained only for approved periods, disclosed only for approved purposes, and verifiably deleted or returned.
Application boundaries enforce secure headers, input and upload limits, signed capabilities, safe errors, throttling, and external-processing gates.
Changes are version-controlled and must pass automated lint, type, test, build, security, and evidence validation before release.
Vulnerabilities are received, prioritized, remediated to approved targets, independently tested, and exceptions are approved and tracked.
Security-relevant identity, hosting, storage, application, and administrative events are centrally retained, reviewed, and alerted without restricted payloads.
Events are triaged, contained, investigated, recovered, communicated, and reviewed under an approved incident plan.
Critical dependencies, recovery objectives, backups, restoration, and continuity procedures are documented and exercised.
Personnel sign confidentiality obligations, complete security training, receive approved access, and are offboarded promptly.
External model use requires approval, follows a documented provider boundary, minimizes and sanitizes packets, and preserves human review.
Management reviews control operation, exceptions, risks, vendors, access, incidents, vulnerabilities, and corrective actions.
